newsitem.title: USA: Eastman Chemical sees $1 bln in Latam revs.
newsitem.headline: Eastman Chemical sees $1 bln in Latam revs.

text.p: Eastman Chemical Co said on Wednesday it expects investments in Latin America to result in annual revenues of $1 billion within the next decade.
Thomas Smith, president of Eastman's Latin American region, said Eastman's sales in Latin America have almost doubled since 1992, with 1995 sales at $270 million.

Eastman expects increasing revenues from the region to position the company for further growth after the turn of the century, Smith said at the 1996 Latin America Chemcial Markets Conference. The company issued a statement based upon his comments.
The Latin America Region is part of a larger global strategy for Eastman, Smith said.
"Our corporate goals are to have 50 percent of our annual sales and 30 percent of our manufacturing assets outside the United States by the year 2000," he said.
Eastman said Latin America's natural resources, improved economic climate, stronger intellectual property rules and young population will attract investment.

Eastman's investments in Latin America include a plant to make Eastapak PET (polyethylene terephthalate) bottle polymer that began production this year in the Mexican state of Veracruz. A second bottle polymer plant is under construction in Zarate, Argentina.
Eastman Chemical posted 1995 sales of $5 billion and net income of $559 million.
